product: SMAP L4 Global 3-hourly 9 km EASE-Grid Surface and Root Zone Soil Moisture Geophysical Data (SPL4SMGP)

grid_cell.note: cell_lat/cell_lon are the cell centre as written in the SPL4SMGP files

sampling.granule: 03:00-06:00 UTC 3-hourly average (granule centre 04:30 UTC, 12:30 Philippine time)
sampling.statistic: mean of the samples in each year-month, then mean, p20, p80 across years per calendar month (linear-interpolated percentiles)

power_compare.label: NASA POWER GWETROOT (model root-zone soil wetness): a different quantity
power_compare.quantity: degree of saturation, 0 = dry, 1 = saturated, unitless
power_compare.not_comparable_note: GWETROOT is a fraction of saturation, SMAP sm_rootzone is volumetric water content (m3/m3). They are not the same number and should not be subtracted or plotted on one axis without saying so.
power_compare.statistic: mean of the daily values per calendar month (copied from lanao-norte-demo-1.json monthly.rootzone_wetness)

provenance.source: NASA NSIDC DAAC, SPL4SMGP Version 8, variables sm_surface and sm_rootzone
provenance.citation: Reichle, R., De Lannoy, G., Koster, R. D., Crow, W. T., Kimball, J. S., Liu, Q. & Bechtold, M. (2025). SMAP L4 Global 3-hourly 9 km EASE-Grid Surface and Root Zone Soil Moisture Geophysical Data . (SPL4SMGP, Version 8). [Data Set]. Boulder, Colorado USA. NASA National Snow and Ice Data Center Distributed Active Archive Center. https://doi.org/10.5067/T5RUATAQREF8 . Subset: cell row 699, col 3254 (EASE-Grid 2.0 9 km), 04:30 UTC granules on days 1, 6, 11, 16, 21, 26 of each month, 2015-04 to 2025-12. Date Accessed 2026-11-14.
provenance.access: NASA Earthdata cloud OPeNDAP (https://opendap.earthdata.nasa.gov), DAP4 CSV subset; granule list from CMR

caveats: SPL4SMGP is a model analysis (the NASA land model with SMAP brightness temperatures assimilated), not a direct satellite reading of this field.

Surface is the top 0-5 cm, root zone is 0-100 cm, both as a 9 km cell average. A single paddy or upland lot can be much wetter or drier than the cell, and irrigation or flooding in the lot is not in the product.
Sampled, not complete: one 3-hour average (03:00-06:00 UTC) on 6 days per month. Monthly values are means of those samples.
The point sits about 320 m from the west edge and about 550 m from the north edge of its 9 km cell, so lots a few hundred metres west or north may fall in the neighbouring cell.
SMAP starts 2015-03-31, so this is about 11 years, not the 25 years used for NASA POWER.
